Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 6.pdf ---
SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming online

during the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page. Quality and traceability of the data matter a lot too, since the whole point is feeding
trustworthy numbers into the international climate change conversation, so whatever
comes out the other end needs solid metadata and documentation attached, not just raw
numbers.

Sistema: SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)

Resumo executivo: SLCCI operationalizes the production of climate-quality sea level datasets from multi-mission satellite altimetry archives. It ingests, calibrates, validates, cross-calibrates, archives, reprocesses, documents, and distributes delayed-time sea level products, enabling climate researchers to use traceable and scientifically approved long-term records.

Escopo: The system produces, preserves, documents, and distributes delayed-time sea level climate products derived from satellite altimetry missions.
  Em escopo: Ingestion of altimetry data from registered satellite missions
  Em escopo: Calibration, validation, and cross-calibration of mission data
  Em escopo: Generation of per-mission track products
  Em escopo: Generation of merged gridded climate records
  Em escopo: Archiving of baseline and intermediate processing data
  Em escopo: Reprocessing using revised algorithms or calibration methods
  Em escopo: Quality approval, metadata management, documentation, and product distribution
  Em escopo: Operational monitoring of production executions
  Fora de escopo: Near-real-time delivery for operational ocean forecasting — the initiative is restricted to delayed-time climate products
  Fora de escopo: General-public or commercial customer services — the target audience is the climate research community
  Fora de escopo: Formal IT service management and incident-ticketing frameworks — explicitly excluded from the operating model
  Premissa: PA-01: Satellite altimetry mission data are available to the initiative for ingestion.
  Premissa: PA-02: Existing ocean-data infrastructure can be assessed and reused where suitable.
  Premissa: PA-03: Scientists provide approved algorithm and calibration configurations for operational use.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Scope): Products shall support delayed-time and historical climate applications only.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Cost): The solution shall be sustainable for long-term operation within an approved operating budget [TBD].
  Restrição: REST-03 (Flexibility): The solution shall accommodate new satellite missions and evolving processing algorithms.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Technology): Existing proven ocean-data infrastructure shall be reused where appropriate.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Production Operations Staff (Usuário primário): Monitor production executions, identify failed processing runs, and maintain daily operation of the production line.
  STK-02 - Sea Level Scientist (Usuário primário): Validate scientific processing, define new products, and introduce revised algorithms or calibration methods.
  STK-03 - Product Quality Reviewer (Usuário primário): Review product quality evidence and record approval decisions before release.
  STK-04 - Catalogue and Metadata Manager (Usuário primário): Maintain complete product catalogue entries, metadata, and documentation.
  STK-05 - Climate Researcher (Usuário secundário): Access reliable, documented, and traceable sea level datasets for climate modelling and research.
  STK-06 - ESA Climate Change Initiative (Stakeholder externo): Receive operational, long-term, scientifically credible climate data products.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Delayed-time climate focus: Sea level products are intended for delayed-time processing and reprocessed historical climate records, not for near-real-time operational forecasting.
  RN-002 - Preservation for reprocessing: Baseline source data and intermediate processing data must be retained to support future reprocessing when algorithms or calibration methods change.
  RN-003 - Quality approval before release: A product must receive a recorded quality approval before it is released to climate researchers.
  RN-004 - Product traceability: Released products must include metadata and documentation sufficient to identify their source missions, processing lineage, and scientific context.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Ingest mission altimetry data: The system shall ingest altimetry data from a registered satellite mission. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Calibrate mission data: The system shall calibrate ingested mission data using a selected calibration configuration. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Validate calibrated data: The system shall execute validation checks on calibrated mission data. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Cross-calibrate missions: The system shall apply cross-calibration processing to validated data from multiple satellite missions. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Generate mission track product: The system shall generate a per-mission track product from processed mission data. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Generate merged gridded product: The system shall generate a merged gridded sea level product from cross-calibrated mission data. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Archive baseline data: The system shall archive ingested baseline mission data. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Archive intermediate data: The system shall archive intermediate data generated during processing. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Reprocess historical data: The system shall reprocess archived data using a selected versioned processing configuration. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Record quality approval: The system shall record a quality approval decision for a product version. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Register product metadata: The system shall register metadata for each product version. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Publish product documentation: The system shall publish documentation associated with an approved product version. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Provide approved products: The system shall provide approved product versions for retrieval by climate researchers. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Register satellite mission source: The system shall register a new satellite mission data source using a configurable source definition. [Should have]
  RF-015 - Register processing configuration: The system shall register a versioned processing configuration for use in a production run. [Should have]
  RF-016 - Display production execution status: The system shall display the execution status of each production run to operations staff. [Must have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Functional Suitability) - The system shall retain source mission identifiers, processing configuration version, calibration configuration version, and product version for 100% of released products. | Métrica: 100% of released product records contain all four traceability attributes.
  RNF-002 (Reliability) - The system shall verify the integrity of 100% of archived baseline and intermediate data objects using a checksum generated at archival time. | Métrica: 100% of sampled archived objects match their stored checksum; sample size and schedule are [TBD].
  RNF-003 (Functional Suitability) - The system shall prevent release of a product version when any mandatory metadata field is absent. | Métrica: 0 released product versions have missing mandatory metadata fields; mandatory field list is [TBD].
  RNF-004 (Flexibility) - The system shall enable registration and ingestion testing of a new satellite mission source without modifying the core processing code. | Métrica: 1 representative new mission source is registered and passes an ingestion test with 0 core-code modifications; acceptance dataset is [TBD].

  RNF-006 (Reliability) - The system shall make production execution status available for at least 99.0% of each calendar month, excluding announced maintenance windows. | Métrica: Maximum unplanned status-service unavailability of 7 hours and 18 minutes per calendar month. [TBD]
  RNF-007 (Maintainability) - The system shall document the reuse decision for 100% of assessed existing ocean-data infrastructure components. | Métrica: 100% of assessed components have a recorded decision of reuse or non-reuse with justification; component inventory is [TBD].

  CA-003 - Dado that calibrated mission data are available, quando the validation step is executed, então the system records a validation result of pass or fail for the processing run

  CA-006 - Dado that cross-calibrated data from multiple missions are available, quando a merged gridded product is generated, então the system creates one product version identified as a merged gridded product

  CA-010 - Dado that a product version is under quality review, quando the product quality reviewer records an approval decision, então the system stores the decision, reviewer identifier, and decision timestamp
  CA-011 - Dado that a product version exists, quando the catalogue and metadata manager submits its metadata, então the system stores metadata containing the source mission identifiers, processing configuration version, and product version
  CA-012 - Dado that a product version is approved and its mandatory metadata is complete, quando the catalogue and metadata manager publishes documentation, então the system associates one published documentation record with the approved product version
  CA-013 - Dado that a product version has a recorded approval decision, quando a climate researcher requests the product version, então the system provides the product only when its recorded decision is approved
  CA-014 - Dado that a scientist submits a complete configurable mission source definition, quando the registration is confirmed, então the system creates one registered mission source without modification to the core processing code
  CA-015 - Dado that a scientist submits a processing configuration definition, quando the registration is confirmed, então the system assigns one unique version identifier and makes that version selectable for a production run
  CA-016 - Dado that production runs have recorded execution statuses, quando production operations staff opens the production status view, então the system displays one status value for each recorded production run

Glossário:
  Altimetry data: Satellite-derived measurements used to determine sea surface height and related sea level information.
  Baseline data: Original ingested mission data preserved as the reference input for later processing and reprocessing.
  Calibration: Application of a selected configuration that adjusts mission data for measurement consistency.
  Cross-calibration: Processing that aligns data from different satellite missions to create a consistent multi-mission record.
  Delayed-time: Processing and delivery model for validated historical climate data that does not target near-real-time operational use.
  Merged gridded product: A sea level product combining cross-calibrated observations from multiple missions on a common grid.
  Per-mission track product: A sea level product containing processed measurements associated with an individual satellite mission track.
  Processing configuration: A versioned definition of algorithms and parameters used to execute a processing or reprocessing run.
  Product version: An identifiable release candidate or released instance of a sea level product with recorded processing lineage.

O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.

negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.

A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser

1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.

O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS

 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.

O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com

3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.

 Inclusivity — acessível a pessoas com diferentes capacidades.
 User Assistance — suporte ao usuário.
 Self-Descriptiveness — interface autoexplicativa.

SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming onlineduring the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page.

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present

Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

1.3 Princípios Fundamentais de Qualidade de Requisitos
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual
• Necessário: Existe uma necessidade real que o justifica. Sem o requisito, há uma lacuna de negócio.
• Não ambíguo: Tem uma única interpretação possível. Evitar: 'eficiente', 'fácil', 'rápido', 'amigável'.
• Verificável: Pode ser testado objetivamente com critério mensurável. 'Rápido' não é verificável; '< 2 s' é.
• Singular: Descreve uma única coisa. Nunca usar 'e' ou 'ou' para combinar dois comportamentos em um 
RF.
• Viável: Tecnicamente e financeiramente possível dentro das restrições do projeto.
• Rastreável: Tem origem (stakeholder ou RN) e destino (caso de teste) identificados.
• Completo: Contém todas as informações necessárias para implementação sem consultas adicionais.
• Consistente: Não conflita com nenhum outro requisito do documento.
• Priorizado: Tem um nível de prioridade definido (MoSCoW: Must/Should/Could/Won't).PARTE 2 — Padrões de Escrita por Artefato

3.3 Produtos de trabalho baseados em template (L3)
Os produtos de trabalho baseados em templates são usados para superar algumas das 
deficiências dos produtos de trabalho baseados na linguagem natural, fornecendo 
estruturas pré-definidas para os requisitos.
▪ Os templates de frases fornecem uma estrutura sintática predefinida para uma frase 
que expressa um requisito, especialmente um requisito individual ou uma história de 
usuário.
▪ Os templates de formulário fornecem um conjunto de campos em um formulário, por 
exemplo, para escrever um caso de uso ou um requisito de qualidade mensurável.
▪ Os templates de documento fornecem uma estrutura pré-definida para um 
documento de requisitos.
Vários templates são descritos na literatura. [ISO29148], [MWHN2009], e [Rupp2014]
fornecem templates de frases para requisitos individuais. [Cohn2004] define um template 
de frase muito utilizado para histórias de usuários e [Cock2001] descreve template de 
formulários para casos de uso. [Laue2002] propôs um template para descrição de tarefas. 
[ISO29148] e [RoRo2012] fornecem template de documentos para especificações 
completas. Além disso, um cliente pode prescrever o uso de templates específicos do 
cliente em um projeto.
Vantagens de produtos de trabalho baseados em template:
▪ Fornecer uma estrutura clara e reutilizável
▪ Ajudar na captura de informações mais relevantes
▪ Fazer com que os requisitos e as especificações dos requisitos pareçam uniformes
▪ Melhorar a qualidade geral dos requisitos e especificações dos requisitos
Desvantagens e armadilhas dos produtos de trabalho baseados em template:
▪ As pessoas comumente se concentram na conclusão formal do modelo e não no seu 
conteúdo.
▪ Os aspectos que não estão incluídos no template são mais prováveis de serem 
omitidos.
3.4 Produtos de Trabalho Baseados em Modelos (L3)
Os requisitos representados em linguagem natural têm limitações [Davi1993], em particular 
no que diz respeito a obter uma visão geral de um conjunto de requisitos e compreender as 
relações entre eles. A modelagem de requisitos atende a essas limitações.

- The system is part of ESA's Climate Change Initiative (CCI), one of about eleven parallel projects each covering a different climate variable.
- The system must take an existing science prototype/production setup and turn it into an operational, day-to-day system.
- The system ingests altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
- The system performs calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions.
- The system produces two product types: a per-mission along-track product and a merged multi-mission gridded product.
- The system must include an archive to preserve baseline and intermediate data, since reprocessing will happen repeatedly.
- Internal users include scientists (deeper validation/product definition), quality reviewers who sign off on products, catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests).
- External users are the climate research community, not the general public or commercial customers.
- Near-real-time (NRT) delivery is explicitly out of scope; the system is delayed-time / reprocessed-data only.
- Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (e.g. ITIL-style) are explicitly out of scope.
- The system must be cost-sustainable to operate long-term, not just a one-off build.
- The system must be flexible enough to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time.
- The system should reuse existing proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
- Output data must include solid metadata and documentation to ensure quality and traceability.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A satellite mission source and a processing configuration are registered.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Mission data are ingested, calibrated, validated, and archived with a recorded execution status.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The processing run is recorded as failed and no product is released.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor starts a production run for a registered mission.
2. The system ingests the mission altimetry data.
3. The system calibrates the ingested data using the selected configuration.
4. The system executes validation checks on the calibrated data.
5. The system archives the baseline and intermediate data.
6. The system records the execution status as completed.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. Validation identifies a non-conforming result → the system records the validation result and marks the run for scientific review.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Data ingestion fails → the system records the execution status as failed and preserves any already archived data (ref. RF-001, RF-007).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Validated data from at least two missions are available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A merged gridded product version is generated.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No merged product version is generated.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects validated mission datasets.
2. The system applies cross-calibration processing.
3. The system generates a merged gridded sea level product.
4. The system records the product version and processing lineage.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The actor selects one mission dataset → the system rejects merged-product generation and requests at least two mission datasets.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Cross-calibration processing fails → the system marks the execution as failed and does not generate a product version (ref. RF-004, RF-006).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Archived baseline data and a versioned processing configuration are available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A new product version is generated from archived data.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: Archived baseline data remain unchanged and no new product version is released.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects archived data and a versioned processing configuration.
2. The system retrieves the archived data.
3. The system executes reprocessing using the selected configuration.
4. The system creates a new product version with processing lineage.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The actor selects a configuration already used for the same dataset → the system displays the existing product version.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Archived data integrity verification fails → the system stops reprocessing and records the failed execution (ref. RN-002, RF-009).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A product version has quality evidence, registered metadata, and documentation.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The approved product version is available for researcher retrieval.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The product version remains unavailable for researcher retrieval.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor reviews the product quality evidence.
2. The actor records an approval decision.
3. The system records the approval decision.
4. The system publishes the associated documentation.
5. The system makes the approved product version available for retrieval.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The actor records a rejection decision → the system retains the product version as not released.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. Mandatory metadata is absent → the system prevents publication and identifies the product version as incomplete (ref. RN-003, RN-004, RF-011).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: At least one approved product version is available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The researcher obtains the selected approved product version and its documentation.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects an approved product version.
2. The system verifies the product approval status.
3. The system provides the product version.
4. The system provides the associated documentation.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The actor selects a per-mission track product → the system provides the selected track product.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The selected version is not approved → the system denies retrieval and displays its release status (ref. RN-003, RF-013).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor has a mission source definition.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A new mission source is registered for ingestion testing.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No new mission source is registered.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor submits a configurable mission source definition.
2. The system validates the source definition.
3. The system registers the mission source.
4. The system records the mission source as available for ingestion testing.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The source definition duplicates an existing mission source → the system displays the existing registration.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The source definition is incomplete → the system rejects registration and identifies the missing fields (ref. RF-014).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The actor has an approved processing configuration definition.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A versioned processing configuration is available for selection in production runs.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No configuration version is available for production selection.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor submits a processing configuration definition.
2. The system assigns a version identifier.
3. The system registers the configuration version.
4. The system makes the configuration version selectable for a production run.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The submitted definition matches an existing version → the system displays the existing version identifier.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Version assignment fails → the system does not register the configuration and records the failure (ref. RF-015).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: At least one production run has been started.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The actor views the current recorded status of production runs.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The actor is informed that status information is unavailable.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the production status view.
2. The system retrieves recorded production runs.
3. The system displays the status for each retrieved run.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. No production runs exist for the selected period → the system displays zero recorded runs.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Status information cannot be retrieved → the system displays an availability error (ref. RF-016, RNF-006).

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The system is one of about eleven parallel ESA Climate Change Initiative projects, each covering a different climate variable — this project covers sea level.
Products must go through calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions before being considered consistent.
Reprocessing happens repeatedly as algorithms and calibration methods evolve, so baseline and intermediate data must never be lost.
The target audience is exclusively the climate research community — not the general public or commercial customers.
Near-real-time (NRT) delivery use cases are explicitly excluded — the system only serves the reprocessed/delayed-time data flow.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a scientist, I want to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed, so that scientific quality is maintained as the system evolves.
As a quality reviewer, I want to evaluate and approve products, so that only validated data is released.
As a member of the catalog/metadata team, I want to maintain the product catalog and metadata, so that the data stays discoverable and well-documented.
As a member of the operational staff, I want to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests, so that day-to-day operations keep running.
As a climate research community member, I want to access reliable, well-documented sea level data, so that I can trust it and build my research on it.

As a system operator, I want to reprocess historical data when algorithms or calibration methods improve, without losing baseline or intermediate data, so that the climate record stays accurate over time.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Process satellite altimetry data — the system ingests data from multiple missions, calibrates and validates it, cross-calibrates between missions, and generates the per-mission and multi-mission gridded products.
Review and release product — a quality reviewer evaluates a newly generated product and approves it for release, or flags it for correction.
Reprocess historical data — an operator triggers reprocessing of archived baseline/intermediate data using an updated algorithm or calibration method, without losing prior data.
Onboard new satellite mission — an operator or scientist configures the system to ingest data from a newly available satellite mission.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given altimetry data from two or more satellite missions, when cross-calibration is performed, then the resulting measurements are consistent across missions.
Given a reprocessing run using an updated algorithm, when processing completes, then the baseline and intermediate data from previous runs remain intact and accessible.
Given a newly generated product, when a quality reviewer evaluates it, then the product is approved for release or flagged for correction.
Given a released dataset, when a climate research community member accesses it, then the dataset includes metadata and documentation sufficient to trace its origin and processing history.
Given a new satellite mission becomes available, when it is onboarded, then that mission's data is processed without requiring a rebuild of the existing processing pipelines.
